SPORTAL Review SPORTAL is what happens when somebody looked at a baseball bat, a hockey stick, a bowling ball, and a pile of B-movie monsters and said: "Yep, that's a first-person shooter." Instead of traditional guns, you're launching spiked baseballs, electrified hockey pucks, exploding golf balls, and bladed bowling balls at hordes of creatures straight out of a 1950s creature feature. The result is a fast-paced arena FPS mixed with roguelite progression and a healthy dose of insanity. The retro pixel-art visuals give off strong boomer-shooter energy, while the roguelite upgrades encourage experimentation with different builds and weapon combinations. The concept is surprisingly original in a genre overflowing with shotguns, demons, and military shooters. The biggest question is whether the gameplay loop stays fresh over dozens of runs. If you're already a fan of arena shooters, roguelites, and over-the-top action, SPORTAL looks like it has all the ingredients to become a hidden gem.

Played the demo for a couple of hours and I definitely wanted more out of it, and the complete version did not disappoint. Progression is fairly easy, and you can pretty much fill the skill tree in a couple of hours to make it a bit more manageable, it definitely comes to a point where the game might get feel too easy the more you keep progressing, but that definitely does not take anything away from the overall experience. Overall, a pretty solid, enjoyable game, mindless fun, and fairly priced for what it has to offer.

[u]Sportal[/u] feels like a Friday night in October 1998. Halloween is right around the corner, your favorite sports-ball team won a big rivalry game, an extra cheese pizza is en route, and your bedroom window is slightly ajar to feel that crisp autumn breeze. The vibes are immaculate with this one. Weapon variety covers most of the bases. Baseball bats, hockey sticks, footballs, lacrosse sticks, golf clubs, frisbees, representing most, not all sports. The arenas are tight, intimate spaces with some being larger than others, but each wave feels fresh with the abundance of mutators that add some spice. I encountered a few bugs i.e. getting stuck on pipes, enemies still moving while I selected my next upgrade, and a couple of seemingly random deaths. Even considering it's flaws I confidently recommend this for any fan of old-school arena shooters with some sports flare. While not a grand slam, Sportal is a three-base hit. With a few tweaks this could easily be a home-run.

Listen, it's 5-7 hours of fun for a fair price. It reminds me of the days when you could rent a game and beat it in the same weekend. I liked the idea of the card/gear system, but will say the bowling ball is generally OP. It also seemed a little too easy once you got about 15% of the ability tree mastered. I think the levels could use some enemies in towers/windows to make the player think harder about their movement. Would also like to see certain enemies immune to certain weapons, make the players have to focus in on a certain build. Take advantage of the small levels by turning up the heat! And lastly a new game plus (more enemies higher health/ more levels stronger gear) or a horde/wave based mode would be sick. All in all, the price makes this game easy to recommend. If you like Nightmare reaper and Smash TV, this may be as close to a perfect storm as you may ever find. Also some of the songs on the OST ball pretty hard. You can definitely feel the DUSK/Quake inspiration from these guys. Can't wait for an update, or their next release. Great work!

Don't expect good level design though, it's only very basic and small arenas here in Sportal. https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3752724291 It took me less than three hours to complete an entire run and kill all the bosses, I hope the developers will add more content if possible.
